Kaleidoscope: Which kaleidoscope pattern is it?
Kaleidoscope. The board has 9x9 sites (144x144 cells). The window shows one site; each move goes to the next site (up, down, left or right). One large kaleidoscope pattern fills the board: its centre in the middle, one spoke piece up and to the right of the centre, and one rim piece at the lower left edge. Every other site is plain. The pattern may sit one site further left or right. Question: Which kaleidoscope pattern is it? The answer is one of eight patterns: snowflake = a solid centre dot, straight spokes, a rim of points; starburst = a hollow centre circle, straight spokes, a rim of points; wheel = a solid centre dot, straight spokes, a rim of round bumps; cross = a hollow centre circle, straight spokes, a rim of round bumps; diamond = a solid centre dot, curved spokes, a rim of points; web = a hollow centre circle, curved spokes, a rim of points; petal = a solid centre dot, curved spokes, a rim of round bumps; ring = a hollow centre circle, curved spokes, a rim of round bumps. Answer with its name. You may answer at any time; you do not need to see every site. Score: 20 if the answer is right, minus 10, minus 0.1 per move (movement budget 35).
The answers: 1 = snowflake, 2 = starburst, 3 = wheel, 4 = cross, 5 = diamond, 6 = web, 7 = petal, 8 = ring.
You see the board, 9 x 9 sites, only through a window of one site (16 x 16 cells). A move goes to the next site. At most 35 moves.
